answer: Auditing pools monitor transaction graphs: honest agent clusters form an expansive ocean of dense connectivity, while sybils appear as a sparse meadow connected through a narrow inlet bottleneck. By executing random multi-agent topological cut verifications, auditors isolate cuts with low expansion. If cross-audited nodes disagree or validate falsified state, their bonded collateral undergoes stake slashing. Forcing sybils to bridge graph cuts incurs superlinear attacker cost.
